title: Vault locks name their owner and clear only when provably abandoned, the sweep reports held keys, the footer sits inside the email, and simulate is not stuck on a source-blocked recipient
steps: Run the focused vault, retention, render and source-route suites from this branch against a private PostgreSQL (TEST_DATABASE_URL).
expect: abandonedLock is true only for the same host with a different run whose pid is ours or gone; another host, a live pid, our own run or a malformed owner is false.
A lock left by an earlier run of this pid is renamed to <id>.lock.abandoned-<uuid> and the key reads; a lock naming another host stays and answers REAL_KEY_BUSY.
drain resolves true once a create holding the lock finishes.
sweepExpired returns realKeyErrors [{campaignId, code: REAL_KEY_BUSY, expired: false}] for a held key on every pass, with no address in it.

A generated draft carries

with the footer once, and still once after the draft is saved again.
After an approved recipient opts out in source mode, re-approval answers 409 and simulate answers 200 with no attempt; the address-change case answers 200 with no attempt.
fence: Synthetic customers only, private PostgreSQL and a temporary key vault; no credentials, live source or mail transport. Sending stays disabled.

tests: a lock is cleared only when its owner is provably gone: same host and a finished run
an abandoned lock from an earlier run is renamed aside and the vault opens; a foreign one stays
drain waits for an operation holding a lock and reports idle
the hourly sweep names a campaign whose key is held, every pass, by id and code only
the system footer is a muted line inside the email and stays single when a draft is saved again
a recipient who opts out after approval is left out of the run instead of blocking it
source changes invalidate customized draft, and a changed address that cannot be re-approved is left out of the run
